title: Priority degradation limiter for multi-region routing
creator: Asha Menon
description: Problem: During regional pressure events we observe abrupt cross-region evacuations that cause a spike in end-to-end tail latency and increased token cost due to repeated hedging. Current geo-pinning and naive failover can move large fractions of traffic at once, violating customer latency SLOs and producing cascading circuit trips. Goal: implement a controller (Priority Degradation Limiter, PDL) that smooths regional failover and limits the rate and magnitude of cross-region degradations while remaining capacity-aware and latency-forward. PDL will sit in the global request director and apply per-route degradation budgets and epochal capacity reservoirs to steer traffic in a controlled way.
design_decisions: Use an epoch window (default 30s) with a per-region capacity reservoir token bucket. Reservoir tokens represent allowed cross-region evacuation volume for that epoch.

Degradation is modeled as a prioritized queue: routes have priority bands (P0..P3). Higher priority routes reserve a fraction of the reservoir; lower priorities are subject to proportionate throttling.

Latency-first routing: PDL uses 95th percentile request latency signals computed per-region+model and weights candidates by latency_score * capacity_budget. If a candidate is saturated or has insufficient reservoir, weight is reduced gracefully instead of hard eject.
Circuit-breaker integration: when a downstream region trips its circuit (observability >= threshold), PDL increases local shedding factor and decays reservoir refill rate to avoid oscillation.
Backpressure vs immediate shed: prefer graceful degradation (probabilistic shedding + slower reroute) over hard failover to reduce thundering herd and preserve SLOs for priority routes.
Config surface: expose per-customer and per-route budget multipliers so Dedicated/Private tenants can tune conservatism. Default for hosted customers tuned for balanced latency and cost.
Telemetry-first rollout: require detailed telemetry before increasing aggressiveness. Default rollout will start with passive mode (observe only) then 10% traffic slow-roll to 100%.
Safety: PDL will not re-route more than X% (default 30) of a route's traffic out of a home-region in a single epoch unless explicitly overridden by ops.
Operational escape hatch: allow immediate global disable flag and per-region quarantine (manual ops override).
implementation_steps: 1) Prototype: add PDL decision function in request director codepath (node: director/pdl) behind feature flag pdl.alpha. Implement reservoir token bookkeeping and epoch loop.

2) Signals ingestion: wire region-level latency q95, concurrency, and capacity-utilization metrics into director via existing telemetry bus (topic: director.metrics). Add a small in-memory moving window aggregator for q95 to avoid dependency on long ETL.
3) Policy config: schema for per-route priority bands, budget multipliers, and max-epoch-eject-percentage. Add validation and defaulting in API layer.
4) Circuit integration: subscribe to region circuit state changes (circuit service) and adjust PDL config dynamically when circuits open/close.
5) Tests: unit tests for token bucket logic, property tests for reservoir exhaustion behavior, integration tests with synthetic latency/capacity emulation.
6) Canary: deploy to staging director with recorded-traffic replay; run chaos scenarios (region degradation, sudden capacity drop) and compare to baseline routing behavior.
7) Gradual rollout: passive-observe -> 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% across selected orgs over 3 weeks, validating telemetry and SLA deviations at each step.
8) Docs & Console: add console UI for per-route budget tuning and a visualization of reservoir usage and epoch events. Write runbook for ops.
9) Post-roll: run 2-week guardrail evaluation, tune defaults, and promote pdl.alpha -> pdl.v1.
testing_plan: Unit: token bucket edge cases (refill under burst, exhaustion, fractional tokens)
Property tests: probabilistic shedding distribution over many epochs matches configured ratios
Integration: replayed traffic with injected latency to a region; verify PDL smooths evacuation and keeps p95/p99 within SLOs for P0 routes
Chaos: simulate circuit flips and capacity drops; verify no >2x traffic spikes to non-home regions and no repeated immediate back-and-forth routing within cooldown window
Load tests: synthetic high-throughput to validate minimal CPU/latency overhead of PDL decision path (target <2% added director latency)
Security: config validation fuzzing and RBAC checks for per-customer overrides
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature flag behind pdl.alpha (off in prod). Deploy director code with metrics-only instrumentation.
Phase 1: Passive observe mode in prod for 72h (no routing changes) collecting reservoir and candidate-weight traces.
Phase 2: Enable active routing at 1% traffic for non-critical routes; monitor p95/p99 and reservoir utilization.
Phase 3: Expand to 10% over 3 days; run targeted failure drills (region latency increase). If regressions > 5% SLOs for P0, rollback to passive.
Phase 4: 50% then 100% after 2-week observation and config tuning. Flip feature flag to pdl.v1 and deprecate pdl.alpha.
Ops manual override: global.disable and region.quarantine are actionable via Console and CLI with audit logging.
telemetry_and_alerting: Dashboards: PDL Overview (reservoir heatmap, per-route eject charts, priority SLO deltas)
Alerts: SLO-regression alert when P0 p95 increases >10% over baseline for 15m, pdl.reservoir.starvation if reservoir refill rate < threshold for 3 epochs
On-call runbook: steps to assess if PDL is causing regressions, how to use global.disable and region.quarantine, links to traces and recent epoch logs
Retention: keep per-epoch traces for 14 days to support post-incident analysis
acceptance_criteria: PDL running in passive mode with correct telemetry for at least 72h
Unit and integration tests covering token bucket, probabilistic shedding, and circuit interactions are green
Canary 1% shows no >5% regressions on P0 p95/p99; ops confirms runbook usability
Load test shows <2% average additional director latency at target QPS
Console UI exposes per-route budget and shows near-real-time reservoir usage
Documentation and a post-roll tuning guide are published in Confluence
